description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number of biomedical entities and the accuracy (ACC %) of various model editing methods, as evaluated in the context of long-tail biomedical knowledge. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to approximately 10⁴ on a logarithmic scale, with major ticks at 10⁰ (1), 10¹ (10), 10² (100), 10³ (1000), and 10⁴ (10000), though the plot only extends to just beyond 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 85% with tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, and 85. Six methods are compared: Base (black solid line with circular markers), FT (blue solid line with downward-pointing triangular markers), IKE (red solid line with upward-pointing triangular markers), MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers), MEMIT (purple solid line with circular markers), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). All methods show increasing accuracy as co-occurrence number increases. ROME starts at approximately 74.5% at co-occurrence ~1 and rises to ~82.5% at ~10³. MEND begins at ~71% and reaches ~80.5%. MEMIT starts at ~70% and climbs to ~77.5%. IKE begins at ~68% and ends at ~75.5%. FT starts at ~65.5% and ends at ~73%. Base starts at ~64% and ends at ~71%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods across the range, while Base consistently underperforms.
